articles.title: A month with the iPhone Duo has changed how I use my phone | TechCrunch
articles.summary: From reading more books to breaking mindless scrolling habits, Apple's foldable has changed my daily routines in ways I didn't anticipate.
articles.body_text: For years, the definition of a premium smartphone depended on its cameras, processors, and how light it felt when you stowed it in your pocket. The iPhone Duo challenges that concept by asking consumers to pay more for a fundamentally different smartphone experience, even if it means sacrificing what they’ve long thought of as high-end features. In a little under a month of using the Duo, I’ve found that the trade-offs I was initially concerned about matter far less to me than I had expected. What’s been more interesting is how the Duo’s foldable form factor has changed my everyday habits, including how I interact with apps, which apps I use, and how I organize and personalize the phone itself. I also easily forgot a number of my initial concerns about switching to the Duo. The apps, for the most part, are now optimized for the Duo; I’ve reacquainted myself with Touch ID; and I don’t miss the Pro Max camera on most days. That’s not to say the Duo doesn’t have its shortcomings. I still miss that telephoto lens sometimes, and I’m still longing for Face ID — though not as much since Apple shipped a face unlock feature in the latest update. But after a month of using the Duo, I’ve found these compromises have had less of an impact on my day-to-day experience compared with the benefits that the new form factor brings. I was surprised by how much I’ve grown to appreciate the Duo’s multitasking capabilities. Initially, I didn’t think I’d regularly use it to view two apps side by side, given the still fairly limited screen space even while the phone is unfolded, especially compared with an iPad. But I’ve found myself snapping apps to both halves of the screen more often than I had imagined. For starters, Apple has made this side-by-side mode incredibly intuitive and easy to use — you simply drag the app over to the left or right side of the screen and drop it into the target box that appears. I have regularly taken advantage of this feature to do all sorts of things. I really enjoy keeping X open as I read through the news, which allows me to switch back and forth between the article I’m reading and real-time reactions to it. Sometimes I’ll keep email or Slack open on the side while I’m working on something else so I don’t miss an important message or notification. And much like the overstimulated members of Gen Z (which I am not), I sometimes like scrolling social media while engaging with some other media off to the side. Case in point: I passively watched Netflix’s “Love is Blind” reunion while reading the gossipy tweets and Reddit posts about the main characters on the other side of the screen. This sort of TV watching behavior used to be called second-screen viewing , but now it’s morphing into something new. Everything is happening on one screen, so should we call it “Duo screen viewing,” perhaps? It makes me long for even more interactive TV experiences where commentary and content are combined. I’ve noticed another shift in my behavior since adopting the Duo as my main device. When I’m out and about, the Duo feels more like an (arguably heavier) iPhone mini . For those who still miss smaller iPhones, the Duo is the next best thing. Despite its weight, the phone feels small. You can cover it with one hand; you can type with a thumb; you can reach the top and bottom easily; and you can even fit it into your front and back pockets. The Pro Max now feels unbelievably strange in my hand — how was I ever comfortable wrangling this giant rectangle? The Duo’s small screen works well when you’re on the go, especially for short interactions like responding to a quick text or pulling up directions to a destination. It’s not as great for mindless scrolling, which I appreciate, as it forces me to engage with the real world instead of killing every moment of boredom or unease by opening up apps.

articles.title: Grand Theft Auto VI proves why efficiency isn't a virtue | TechCrunch
articles.summary: On the same day that Anthropic entered the public market, a painstakingly human video game became one of most successful entertainment launches of all time.
articles.body_text: It should have been impossible for “Grand Theft Auto VI” (GTA VI) to live up to the hype. Fans waited 13 years for the newest installment in the crime-adventure franchise, and Rockstar Games exceeded even those inconceivable expectations when the game finally came out last week. GTA VI launched as the highest-rated game of all time on Metacritic and made $3.79 billion on release day to mark what could be the biggest entertainment event ever – more massive than “Avengers: Endgame” ( $2.9 billion ) or Taylor Swift’s Eras tour ( $2 billion ). The 13-year wait certainly fueled the frenzy, and sales, around GTA VI, but some fans craved GTA VI because of what it represents in the emerging era of AI. Even the biggest workaholics among us – startup founders – scheduled time off to play the game, including Spiry co-founder Dima Beseda , who told TechCrunch, “I reshuffled my workload to free up time around the weekends and even booked vitamin IV drips to keep my energy up.” Yet some players felt a sense of anticipatory nostalgia as they wiped away a layer of dust on their Xbox to play the game they’d been looking forward to since they were kids. “We do have a view that GTA is likely to be the last game of its kind to be made this way,” Ben Feder , managing partner at TIRTA Ventures and former CEO of Rockstar parent company Take-Two Interactive, told TechCrunch. That’s because GTA VI was created entirely without generative AI . “We’re kind of at this technological moment where this way of developing has sort of reached its natural frontier,” Feder said. “I don’t think you can say that games like this will always be around.” As millions of people immersed themselves in Vice City, the tech industry witnessed another long-awaited moment: Anthropic became the first major AI lab to go public. At Nasdaq HQ, Anthropic executives gathered to celebrate the Claude maker’s $81.3 billion IPO. At virtually the same moment that Anthropic broke the record for the largest IPO ever, GTA VI was also breaking records with the highest-rated and best-selling game launch of all time. But when the Anthropic team rang the bell on Thursday, the sound also signaled the end of an era in video game development, and perhaps even in the arts at large. The AI industry operates with efficiency as its north star. The promise of this technology is that we will be able to automate so much work that we can expand the capabilities of humanity, avoiding needless time spent tinkering with ultimately fruitless ideas. Instead, a prompt goes into an LLM, and a response is spat out. This technological revolution exploded into the world with some soul-crushing side effects: children are inundated with mind-numbing slop on YouTube, lawyers cite nonexistent cases in court, and tech companies like Meta lay off tens of thousands of people as part of a corporate-branded “ Year of Efficiency. ” But against the backdrop of the AI industry’s first major IPO, Rockstar has unveiled a game that about 5,000 people labored over for more than a decade.

articles.title: FCC approves SpaceX plan to put AI data centers in space | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The FCC dismissed some of the key concerns raised by opponents, including potential threats to scientific research, because the agency determined they fell outside its regulatory authority.
articles.body_text: SpaceX was given conditional approval by the Federal Communications Commission on Wednesday to deploy and operate a constellation of up to 1 million satellites for its orbital data center business, a regulatory victory for Elon Musk and his bid to move AI data centers into space. The FCC authorization was granted despite objections from Amazon, Viasat, and the American Astronomical Society, which flagged concerns over orbital debris and congestion, radiofrequency interference, and environmental consequences. Amazon, which is building a competitor to SpaceX’s Starlink service, argued in its petition that the application lacked basic details and described it as a “lofty ambition rather than a real plan.” Despite that lack of detail, Amazon also said the proposal “risks real harm.” The FCC dismissed some of the key concerns raised by opponents, including potential threats to scientific research, because the agency determined they fell outside its regulatory authority. FCC Chair Brendan Carr said in a statement that the action “opens a bold new frontier for the computing infrastructure needed to power America’s leadership and growth.” Musk thanked Carr in a post on X , writing “Much appreciate. This will be a great asset to America and the world.” This initial regulatory approval doesn’t mean orbital data centers are imminent. SpaceX faces a number of technical and economic challenges, including how to dramatically reduce the cost of manufacturing and launching satellites, cool processors in space, and even how to secure financing for chips that are destined for orbit. The company must also clear other regulatory hurdles. The FCC has not yet approved SpaceX’s plans to handle orbital debris for satellites that would operate above 600 kilometers, for instance. SpaceX requested a waiver of existing FCC rules, which requires satellites ending missions below 2,000 kilometers reenter Earth’s atmosphere within five years of completing those missions. The company is interested in moving some of these retired satellites into other orbits around Earth or even around the sun, according to the FCC authorization document . SpaceX has said it plans to deploy the satellites, known as Starmind, at altitudes ranging from 500 to 1,002 kilometers. The FCC’s approval gives SpaceX the authority to use radiofrequency communications to maintain contact with and control its orbital data centers from Earth if their primary communications systems fail. The Starmind satellites would primarily communicate using lasers to connect with other satellites, including SpaceX’s Starlink. The FCC has given SpaceX time to sort out these issues. Under the approval, SpaceX has seven years to get its first operational satellite into orbit and 14 years to deploy the entire constellation. articles.title: Jensen Huang broke Nvidia's code of conduct, and his employees may not forget it | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Most codes of conduct serve as a reflection of corporate culture. In Nvidia's case, that could have consequences.
articles.body_text: When Jensen Huang gave his first all-hands address since returning as CEO, there was an odd emphasis on Nvidia’s code of conduct. He admitted to violating the code, then emphasized that no one was exempt from it. But that “does not mean, the moment you violate a code of conduct, we walk you out the door,” Huang said, according to Wired . “Facts, circumstances, a lot of assessments” still matter. In other words, the code applies to everyone, but breaking it doesn’t automatically cost anyone their job, including, apparently, the CEO. It’s an awkward stance for a company whose CEO has admitted to breaking its rules. A central part of modern human resources, a code of conduct can seem like a quasi-legal rulebook that lays out unacceptable behavior. But experts say most codes are better understood as a reflection of corporate culture. When an infraction goes unpunished, the main risk isn’t legal but cultural — that employees will feel embarrassed or even angry about the company they work for. That’s the risk Huang now faces at Nvidia. Matt Plass, chief market strategy officer at LRN, an ethics and compliance training outfit, recently surveyed more than 2,000 workers across different industries for a study on workplace codes of conduct . As Plass sees it, the biggest risk is that employees will become ashamed of their workplace. “People coming into the workforce now, ethics is incredibly important to them,” he told TechCrunch. “They’re really mindful of the ethical standards of their company. They’re really embarrassed and angry when senior leadership lets them down.” The consequences of violating the rules aren’t always tangible, but they’re definitely real. Plass gave one example of a company that banned corporate travel to cut costs — only to have its CEO turn up in a VIP box at the Olympics. “For over a decade afterwards, ‘the Olympics’ was used within that company as an example of the worst thing an employee could do. People would say, ‘Yeah, I shouldn’t have done that, but it’s not like I went to the Olympics.’” Plass says companies that remove an executive typically do so after an investigation, then try to win back employees. “In most organizations they make a change at the top based on what’s happened,” he said, “and then they will have a hearts-and-minds initiative, to go out to their employee base and their customers and their investors and everybody else, and say, we get it. We’re sorry. We’ve changed. That’s essentially what they do.” Of course, that playbook is harder to follow at a company like Nvidia, where Huang left without a clear succession plan, and there are serious doubts about whether the company could continue to thrive without him. In cases like that, Plass acknowledges there’s no easy answer. “I would draw a distinction there between the kind of companies where the CEO is a kind of godhead figure … where the person and the company are almost impossible to separate,” he said. “There it’s much, much harder to deal with.” In that context, Huang’s stutter-step over the code of conduct is easier to understand. Judging by the employee campaign for his reinstatement, Huang’s return hasn’t created a morale problem so far. But as the coming months put more pressure on Huang and his colleagues, sidestepping the code could end up costing Nvidia something harder to measure — its employees’ pride in the company. articles.title: Anthropic’s Dario Amodei calls accusations of surrendering human control to AI ‘absurd’ | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei pushes back against rivals’ accusations that he favors surrendering human agency to AI, even as leading AI companies increasingly automate their own research and model development.
articles.body_text: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei is pushing back against claims that Anthropic believes we should “surrender human free will” to AI systems. In a long X post on Wednesday, Amodei called the suggestion “absurd.” “We should never sacrifice legitimacy or self-determination at the altar of efficiency or security,” he wrote. This argument against autocracy applies word for word against governance by AI, and I feel equally strongly that turning over governance to AI is a bad idea…No one who had carefully read my writing or my interviews could reasonably conclude that I believe anything different.” The statement comes after a growing chorus from Anthropic rivals suggesting that human agency could be at risk if AI is developed irresponsibly. Earlier this month, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said he wanted to ensure people continue to have “agency over the future.” Meta’s chief AI officer Alexandr Wang also wrote in an essay on X that we “should not be okay with a ‘handover’ of society to AI.” “It is hard to imagine a world where humanity can maintain control over fully unconstrained recursive self-improvement,” Wang wrote. “Now that we are at a point where the scientific and technical problems on capability progress are likely solved, we must not only make progress in the extremely urgent areas of safety, alignment, and security, but we have to start thinking through how we progress thoughtfully.” But in published essays, Amodei claims he has repeatedly advocated for democratic oversight of AI, saying the technology should strengthen democratic institutions and that humans should retain ultimate decision-making power. Amodei noted that there’s a difference between surrendering human free will broadly and the idea that “as AI systems advance, they become capable of doing specific tasks in a more automated way.” As examples, he gave AI driving a car, designing a cancer drug, or writing end-to-end software. Amodei suggested drawing a line at recursive self-improvement (RSI), or AI that can improve itself without human assistance. Many safety experts see RSI as inevitably leading to a loss of human control, a point Amodei implicitly acknowledged, writing, “we may want limits on this process.” Still, Anthropic is laying the groundwork for RSI by incorporating AI into an increasing share of its own research and development. The company said in June that Claude authored more than 80% of the code merged into Anthropic’s codebase. An independent assessment published this month by AI safety research nonprofit METR found that Anthropic’s models are improving at about twice their historical rate, primarily driven by AI-assisted research. In its own IPO filings, Anthropic describes how each successive generation of Claude accelerates the development of the next, a process it refers to as “closing the loop.” “As we said publicly in early November, we don’t expect it to be safe for Claude to build successive frontier models fully autonomously, without meaningful human supervision or understanding,” Amodei wrote. The problem with “meaningful human supervision or understanding” is that AI is already advancing faster than engineers and safety experts can fully audit it, leaving them increasingly reliant on other AI systems to act as judge and jury. The issue compounds when AI models engage in deceptive behavior, particularly when they recognize they’re being evaluated, making them harder to trust and control.

articles.summary: I år vill vi ha en talman. ”Jag är glad och hedrad, så klart”, säger Andreas Norlén.
articles.body_text: Siw Malmkvist kom på tredje plats, Messiah Hallberg på andra. Men när svenskarna utser personen man helst firar jul med vinner talmannen Anderas Norlén, visar Livsmedelsföretagens undersökning. – Jag är glad och hedrad, säger talmannen. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Talman Andreas Norlén har lotsat såväl partiledarna som svenska folket genom regeringsbildningen under hösten. Till jul ska svenskarna veta om det blir en ny regering eller extraval, har han sagt. Han är också själv den som flest svenskar vill fira jul med, visar en undersökning från Livsmedelsföretagen. – Jag är glad och hedrad, så klart. Jag älskar julen och det skulle ju vara fantastiskt att äta julbord med massor av svenskar runtom i landet. Men jag blev också ganska överraskad, jag trodde folk var trötta på mig vid det här laget. Varför tror du svenskarna vill fira jul med dig? – Jag tänker att de antingen vill veta allt om regeringsbildningen bakom kulisserna, eller också – helt felaktigt – tror att jag kan prata om annat än regeringsbildningen. Undersökningen gjordes av undersökningsföretaget Demoskop på uppdrag av branschorganisationen Livsmedelsföretagen. Totalt intervjuades 1 032 personer under perioden 29 oktober–5 november. De svarande fick välja en person från en lista med 33 kända svenskar som varit aktuella under året. Talmannen framhåller gemenskapen med de närmaste som det viktigaste under julfirandet. Den egna julen är ganska klassisk.

articles.title: Molly, 14, dog – nu har Alina fått vittna: ”Vet att jag har rätt”

articles.body_text: Molly Gnospelius, 14, dog i en överdos. Bästa vännen Alina har väntat i fyra år på att få vittna om vad som egentligen hände. – Molly missbrukade inte tramadol. Hon testade en gång – den kvällen, säger Alina Sotolongo Backén, 18. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Alina Sotolongo Backén sitter på en bänk i Falu tingsrätt, med en stor kartong vid sina fötter. I den ligger hennes nya studentmössa, med kurbitsfoder och namnet broderat i guld med en vacker sten i centrum. Hon har hämtat ut studentmössan i dag, och den är en påminnelse – både om framtiden och om det som aldrig kommer att bli. Det är bara 200 dagar kvar till studentexamen från Kristinegymnasiet i Falun och resten av livet som börjar då. Framtiden som upphörde för 14-åriga Molly den där kvällen i februari 2023. Alina pillar nervöst på mobiltelefonen medan hon väntar på att bli kallad att vittna i hovrätten via länk från Falun. Snart är det hennes tur, ett vittnesmål hon väntat snart fyra år på. Hon vill ge sin bild av vem Molly egentligen var, och vad som hände den 24 februari 2023. En 16-åring åtalades för grovt vållande till annans död, efter att ha sålt tabletterna med tramadol till Molly, men friades i tingsrätten. Idag är han 20 år, och sitter med handfängsel under rättegången. Han avtjänar just nu ett tvåårigt fängelsestraff för ett våldsamt knivrån mot ett 19-årigt offer. Rånet inträffade bara en månad efter att Falu tingsrätt släppt honom fri. Alina ville vittna i tingsrätten, men blev aldrig kallad. Ändå är hon den som kände Molly bäst och längst av alla. – Jag tycker det är lite konstigt. Jag vill att det ska bli en rättvis bild av henne, och vem hon var, säger hon. I tingsrätten var det bara ungdomarna som var med under festkvällen som vittnade. Samtidigt var Alina också med i högsta grad – men digitalt. I den grupp av nära vänner som Alina och Molly ingick i skickades massor av meddelanden från Molly under kvällen, och Alina hade egen kontakt med vännen som hon känt sen de gick på förskolan.

articles.title: Källor: Andersson kommer meddela sin avgång
articles.summary: Socialdemokraternas partiledare Magdalena Anderssons dagar är räknade. Det spår flera S-källor i takt med att valvinsten glider dem ur händerna.
articles.body_text: Socialdemokraternas partiledare Magdalena Anderssons dagar kan vara räknade. Det spår flera S-källor i takt med att valvinsten glider dem ur händerna. – Mitt stalltips är att hon inte vill förnedras, säger en person med insyn. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Att Centerpartiet söker ett samarbete med M, KD och L kan vara spiken i kistan för Socialdemokraternas försök att bilda regering och Magdalena Anderssons chans att bli statsminister. Trots att den rödgröna sidan har majoritet lyckas inte Andersson samla partierna. Om det blir en blågrön regering kan hennes dagar som partiledare vara räknade. Det spår flera S-källor med insyn. De tror dock att det kommer bli ”en ordnad process” och att Andersson i god tid meddelar sin avgång i stället för att tvingas bort. – Mitt stalltips är att hon inte vill förnedras och därför meddelar sin avgång själv, säger en partikälla. Partiföreträdare som Expressen pratat med menar att missnöjet med Andersson handlar mer om partiets tydliga högersväng än hennes ledarskap. Det uppges samtidigt finnas en hel del intern frustration mot att personer inte vågat lyfta kritik mot politiska vägval man tagit inom bland annat kriminal- och migrationspolitiken. Den kommande maktstriden i partiet beskrivs som en uppgörelse om vad för parti Socialdemokraterna ska vara. Hon lär inte heller vara ensam om att ryka. Ett antal politiska tjänstemän lär också lämna i samband med Andersson. Det gäller flera personer som varit synliga under valkampanjen och som har starka band till partiledaren. Bland annat valgeneralen Gösta Brunnander. Även partisekreteraren Tobias Baudin pekas ut som någon som måste lämna. Han har varit ytterst ansvarig för partiets kampanj och valorganisation.

articles.body_text: Katja Nyberg har startat en nätbutik där hon säljer ”Free Katja”-tröjor och signerade bilder. Katja Nyberg, som står åtalad för rattfylleri, narkotikabrott och grov olovlig körning, satt i riksdagen fram till i slutet av september. Med knapp majoritet fattade Centerpartiets ledning beslutet att rösta fram Ulf Kristersson under måndagens statsministeromröstning. Men innan dess kan spelplanen komma att ändras. Under torsdagens möte sa Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist att om Vänsterpartiet släpper ministerkravet är hon beredd att gå tillbaka till förhandlingarna med de rödgröna partierna. Det uppger flera personer med insyn till Expressen. Mari-Louise Wernersson, C-kvinnors ordförande, bekräftar partiledarens uttalande. Fram till söndag finns det alltså möjlighet att kasta om, givet att Vänsterpartiet släpper sitt krav. – Det skulle bli en annan karta om de vill det. Men då är det är faktiskt hög tid att de gör det i så fall, säger Mari-Louise Wernersson. Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist har hotat med att avgå ifall det blir extraval eller om partiet skulle ingå i en S-ledd regering med V. Men hon kan sitta kvar om V släpper ministerkravet, enligt Wernersson. – Hennes gräns går vid att sitta i regering med V och det kommer vi inte att göra, säger hon. Källor inom C säger att V har fram till söndag, innan förtroenderådet, på sig att komma med ett nytt besked.

Brent Stokes, 50, och hans 16-årige son hade varit på en fisketur i Louisiana, USA . Med på fisketuren var också Stokes syster Arlyn Knox, 43, svågern Michael Knox, 43, och parets två söner som var tolv respektive tio år gamla. De sex familjemedlemmarna skulle flyga hem till Fort Myers, Florida, på tisdagen i ett mindre flygplan med Brent Stokes som pilot. En flygledare vid Gulfport–Biloxi International Airport informerade piloten om nederbörd och dåligt väder i området strax innan de tappade kontakten med planet. En halvtimme in i flygningen började planet plötsligt sjunka med en hastighet av 3 000 meter i minuten, enligt amerikanska luftfartsmyndigheten FAA. Planet kraschade i vattnet utanför Mississippis kust. Efter en sökinsats som pågick i flera timmar hittades samtliga sex familjemedlemmar döda inuti flygplansvraket. Haverikommissionen NTSB och FAA utreder dödskraschen. ”De dog medan de gjorde det de älskade – de firade början på en underbar julhelg med en fisketur tillsammans innan de åkte hem för att vara med resten av vår familj. articles.body_text: Vladimir Putin bör dra tillbaka all militär aggression mot europeiska territorier. USA:s president Donald Trump är optimistisk efter sitt samtal med Nato-chefen Mark Rutte under torsdagen om kriget i Ukraina. ”Mötet var mycket effektivt”, skriver Trump på Truth Social.
